# Narrative comparison and rewrite decisions

The requested script overhaul supersedes the previous animation pass's verbatim freeze. The game keeps its cast, places, seven commitments, mechanics and ending choices; its dialogue and causal explanation have been rewritten. Original text is retained in guarded old/new patches under narrative-work/. Existing animation story and voice manifests are regenerated from the revised source rather than silently presenting an old screenplay as current.

## Reference comparison

Square Enix's official Chrono Trigger story synopsis links a fair, a specific accident, a missing companion and the decision to follow her. The useful craft lesson is a chain of visible causes with a person at stake; it is not a license to copy the fair/time-travel plot. Ash & Aether's delivery now leads to Nell's father's theft, Rook's culpability, the workshop plate, the prison rescue, and the departing carriage.

Source: https://www.jp.square-enix.com/chronotrigger/en/story.html

The official Final Fantasy VII Remake synopsis establishes the exploited resource, the opposing company, the resistance and Cloud's immediate operation. The useful comparison is that a player can say who is acting, against whom, and why before learning the whole world. Ash & Aether previously asked the player to operate relays without adequately explaining what they did; rewritten scenes identify the person being helped and the actual effect of the operation. No FFVII names, dialogue or scenes are imported.

Source: https://www.square-enix.com/ffvii/en-us/games/remake/

Square Enix's Final Fantasy X material describes a shared journey whose local stops serve a larger goal. Our practical inference is that a chapter should both resolve a local need and change a relationship, belief or understanding; travel should follow evidence or a promised responsibility. Chapters9–24 therefore continue the consequences of the Crown's fall rather than inventing an unrelated second campaign.

Source: https://na.finalfantasy.com/titles/finalfantasy10

Sabotage's Sea of Stars press kit explicitly describes shifts between epic, silly and emotional material, plus everyday activities in its world. The useful pacing comparison is permission to breathe: home, food, repairs, shelters and the return to Mara should not all speak in final-battle metaphors. This is an editorial inference from the cited descriptions, not a measured claim that our game now matches those games' quality.

Source: https://sabotagestudio.com/presskits/sea-of-stars/

## The dramatic line

Sable wants to finish an ordinary obligation and come home. A stolen voice forces a first choice to help; a recording of his dead mother gives him a personal reason to keep going. He initially looks for one machine to break and one impossible answer to his grief. The reactor victory saves people but does not erase the surrounding harm. The later rescues expose the crew's own complicity and the limits of preserving a voice without a person's permission. Sable eventually chooses repair, shared responsibility and an open future over control. Returning the reed case to Mara pays off the ordinary promise with which the game began. This hero-cycle is the revision's organizing frame, not a new collectible or extra ending condition.

## Dialogue and performance contract

NAME: starts a real spoken turn. Narration does not inherit a preceding speaker's voice. Character portraits follow the current turn. Inventory, learning, party and control receipts use a separate status panel and never enter the voice queue. A missing recording leaves the subtitle visible; it does not invoke robotic browser speech. Audio is matched by exact speaker/text and stopped on page advance, choice, pause, load and close. Music ducks only while a prerecorded line actually plays. Voices cover selected scenes, not the entire campaign.

## Verification limits

The patch receipts verify that only strings changed in the world export; numbers, room coordinates, object types, reward quantities, flags and answer/branch indices are unchanged. Engine/model tests protect reachability and save behavior. These checks cannot certify artistic quality, emotional effectiveness or a complete player experience. A continuous human playthrough and further performance editing remain needed.
